content_units: Best Fit for a CS Student Under $1,200

All three meet your   16GB RAM   minimum and stay within budget. For your mix of   programming, light video editing, occasional gaming, and decent battery life  , the best overall pick is   Lenovo IdeaPad 5 Pro  , with   ASUS TUF A15   second for gaming-heavy use and   MacBook Air M2   third for battery-first users who are okay with limited gaming and macOS-specific tradeoffs.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Laptop   Price   Strengths   Tradeoffs   Best For

1   Lenovo IdeaPad 5 Pro   $999   Strong Ryzen 7 7840HS CPU, sharp 14" 2.8K display, good portability, large 75Wh battery, best value   No dedicated GPU, so gaming/video editing headroom is more limited than ASUS   Most CS students wanting balance

2   ASUS TUF A15   $1,149   Best gaming performance by far, RTX 4050 helps with video editing and GPU workloads, large 90Wh battery   Heaviest by a lot, bulkier, less portable, likely noisier under load   Students who care most about gaming/performance

3   MacBook Air 13 M2   $1,199   Best battery life, lightest premium option, excellent build quality, strong everyday performance   Weakest for gaming, fewer ports, macOS compatibility can be a factor for some classes/tools   Battery-first users who prefer macOS
1) Lenovo IdeaPad 5 Pro
-   Why it ranks first:   It hits the sweet spot of   price, portability, battery, and CPU performance  .
- The   Ryzen 7 7840HS   is excellent for coding, IDEs, Docker, multitasking, and school workloads.
- The   14-inch 2.8K display   is a big plus for reading code and general productivity.
- At   1.46kg  , it is much easier to carry daily than the ASUS.
- At   $999  , it leaves room in your budget for accessories like a monitor, mouse, or external SSD.
Tradeoff:
- Integrated graphics are fine for   light gaming   and casual editing, but not as strong as the ASUS RTX 4050 for AAA games, CUDA workflows, or heavier Premiere/DaVinci tasks.
Bottom line:   Best overall choice for a CS student who wants the least compromise.
2) ASUS TUF A15
-   Why it ranks second:   It is the clear winner for   gaming   and the best for   GPU-accelerated editing  .
- The   RTX 4050   makes a major difference for 1080p gaming and creative apps that benefit from a dedicated GPU.
- The   Ryzen 7 7735HS   is still a strong CPU for programming and coursework.
- The   90Wh battery   is large, though real battery life under gaming/heavier use will drop much faster than the MacBook.
Tradeoff:
- At   2.2kg  , it is much heavier and less pleasant to carry around campus daily.
- The   FHD display   is fine, but less sharp and less premium-feeling than the Lenovo’s 2.8K panel.
- Gaming-laptop thermals, fan noise, and bulk are the cost of that extra performance.
Bottom line:   Choose this if   occasional gaming   is actually important enough to be a priority, not just a nice bonus.
3) MacBook Air 13 M2
-   Why it ranks third:   It offers the   best battery life  , best portability, and a very polished overall experience.
- The   M2   is excellent for coding, web dev, app dev, note-taking, and light creative work.
- At   1.24kg  , it is the easiest to carry.
- Battery life is the strongest here by a noticeable margin.
Tradeoff:
- It is the   worst gaming option   of the three.
- Some CS courses use tools that are easier on Windows, though many development workflows work very well on macOS.
- Fanless design means sustained heavy workloads can throttle sooner than bigger laptops.
Bottom line:   Great if you strongly prefer   macOS + battery life  , but not the best all-around fit for your stated mix.
Tradeoff Guide by Priority
If you want the best overall value
Pick   Lenovo IdeaPad 5 Pro  .
- Best balance of performance, battery, display, weight, and price
- Strong enough for programming, light editing, and casual gaming
- Most sensible student buy
If you want the best gaming and editing performance
Pick   ASUS TUF A15  .
- RTX 4050 is the biggest performance advantage in this group
- Better for GPU-heavy tasks and modern games
- Worth it only if you accept the extra weight and bulk
If you want the best battery life and portability
Pick   MacBook Air M2  .
- Best unplugged laptop here
- Excellent for coding on the go
- Least suitable for gaming and some Windows-first course setups
Final Recommendation
1st place: Lenovo IdeaPad 5 Pro

It is the best match for your priorities in order:   budget, 16GB RAM, decent battery life, strong programming performance, light editing, and occasional gaming  . It gives you the fewest downsides for student life.
2nd place: ASUS TUF A15
Best alternative if your “occasional gaming” is closer to a real priority and you want the extra GPU power.
3rd place: MacBook Air 13 M2
Best for portability and battery, but a more specialized choice unless you already know you want macOS.
